references.text: Describes holding fast to the Lord (דָּבַק) as part of fearing and serving him, using the same verb as in 4:4
Uses the same expression about holding fast to the Lord (וּלְדָבְקָה־בוֹ) as a result of obedience
Exhorts Israel to hold fast to the Lord (וּבוֹ תִדְבָּקוּן) in contrast to following false prophets
Links holding fast to the Lord (וּלְדָבְקָה־בוֹ) directly to life, the same theme as in 4:4
Joshua exhorts the people to hold fast to the Lord (וּלְדָבְקָה־בוֹ) just as Moses did
Refers back to Israel having held fast to the Lord (תִּדְבָּקוּ) until this day
The psalmist expresses that his soul clings to the Lord (דָּבְקָה נַפְשִׁי אַחֲרֶיךָ), showing the same devotion
Barnabas exhorts believers to hold fast to the Lord (προσμένειν τῷ κυρίῳ), a New Testament parallel
Paul exhorts to hold fast to what is good (κολλώμενοι τῷ ἀγαθῷ), a similar principle of faithful attachment
